newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE, Veba up on telecoms deal.
newsitem.headline: RWE, Veba up on telecoms deal.

text.p: A surprise announcement of an imminent alliance on telecommunications between German utility RWE AG and Veba AG and Cable & Wireless boosted both German stocks in early dealings on Wednesday.
"Telecoms are certainly the big news today," said a Frankfurt dealer, of the flurry of activity which followed the early morning announcement.

RWE's common stock was up 1.20 marks, or two percent at 59.10 marks at 0746 GMT while Veba was up 55 pfennigs at 81.65 marks. The stocks were the morning's most heavily traded and outperformed the blue chip DAX index, which was little changed.
Meanwhile Viag AG, with whom RWE had been expected to form an alliance, dropped 16.90 marks, or 2.8 percent, to 587.50 marks.
"The reactions are pretty predictable -- people are getting out of Viag, getting into Veba and RWE," another dealer noted.
RWE surprised the market by revealing it had abandoned plans to form a telecoms alliance with Viag and British Telecom and was in the final stages of talks with Veba and Cable & Wireless.
RWE said it had pulled out of talks with Viag and BT because of differences in market positioning for Germany's planned E2 mobile telephone network.
